content.what_it_is: MATLAB postprocessor that loads five eta snapshots (L6-L16), takes row 2 from each, creates a normalized coordinate from a shared first-file length (L21-L24), filters samples to -2<=x<=20 while normalizing amplitudes by dep (L26-L39), reconstructs the coordinate column (L40-L44), and writes a six-column tab-delimited benchmark file (L46).
entities: dx @L21; loop index i @L22; x @L23; ii @L26; kk @L31; data @L32; ll @L40

equations.ref: first normalized eta column; columns 3-6 repeat for d2-d5
coordinate column reordered to match reverse-selected data rows

unresolved: Cross-file range defect across L7-L16 and L32-L36: n is taken only from eta_0095, but the same index i is applied to d1-d5 without checking that every loaded matrix has at least two rows and n columns; any shorter or differently shaped file causes out-of-range indexing.

Empty-selection defect across L26-L46: if no generated x lies in [-2,20], kk and data are never assigned, yet the later coordinate loop/output still uses data, causing an undefined-variable failure rather than an empty result.
length(d) at L7 selects the largest matrix dimension rather than explicitly the second-row width; an input with more rows than columns makes d1(i) exceed its column count.
The script overwrites d for each load and never checks that all five snapshots share the same spatial grid, so equal lengths with different grids silently produce misregistered columns.
